# relay_documentdb_cluster (Resource)

A managed DocumentDB cluster, MongoDB-compatible on port 27017 with TLS. Creating, updating and destroying wait for the cluster to settle. Changing `name`, `workspace_id` or `version` replaces the cluster and its data; use `lifecycle { prevent_destroy = true }`. DocumentDB has no backups, restore, parameters, storage autoscaling, compute autoscaling or private endpoints yet, and is not available on the Free plan.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "relay_documentdb_cluster" "catalog" {
  workspace_id        = relay_workspace.prod.id
  name                = "catalog"
  version             = "18"
  deletion_protection = true

  storage = {
    size = "40Gi"
  }

  nodes = {
    main = {
      count     = 3
      cloud     = "aws"
      region    = "us-east-1"
      tier      = "R20"
      resources = {}
    }
  }

  default_connections = {
    readonly = true
    admin    = false
  }

  lifecycle {
    prevent_destroy = true
  }
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) Cluster name, unique in the workspace.
- `nodes` (Attributes Map) The cluster's single node group, keyed by a label you choose: one primary and `count - 1` replicas. Renaming it replaces the cluster. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--nodes))
- `workspace_id` (String) Workspace the cluster belongs to.

### Optional

- `default_connections` (Attributes) Relay-managed users the platform creates once the cluster is running, each with a Relay connection that uses it: one read-only and one admin, since DocumentDB grants writes only with administration. Omitted on create, both are created, as the Relay console does; omitted afterwards, the current value is kept. Changing a role on an existing cluster creates it, or deletes its connection and then its user, without replacing the cluster; a user whose roles were changed outside Relay is kept. The platform applies a change after the apply returns. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--default_connections))
- `deletion_protection` (Boolean) While `true`, the platform refuses to delete the cluster, and `terraform destroy` or a replacement fails before deleting it. Turning it on needs deletion protection enabled for the organization. Turning it off needs the `org.deletion_protection.disable` permission, which the owner and admin roles hold.
- `storage` (Attributes) Volume size of every node: each node holds the whole data set. Omit the block and the platform picks the size included with the tier, which the next read reports. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--storage))
- `timeouts` (Block, Optional) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--timeouts))
- `version` (String) DocumentDB version, `17` or `18`. Omit it and the platform picks one, which the next read reports. There is no in-place upgrade: changing it replaces the cluster and its data.

### Read-Only

- `created_at` (String) Creation time, RFC 3339.
- `endpoint_host` (String) Public read-write endpoint host, the same as the `rw` entry of `public_endpoints`. Empty until the platform publishes it.
- `endpoint_port` (Number) Public read-write endpoint port, 27017.
- `id` (String) Cluster ID.
- `phase` (String) Lifecycle phase after the last apply.
- `phase_message` (String) Detail for the phase.
- `public_endpoints` (Attributes List) Public endpoints by role: `rw` for the primary and `ro`, the `<name>-ro` host, for the replicas. Clients connect with `mongodb://<user>:<password>@<host>:27017/?tls=true`. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--public_endpoints))
- `ready_nodes` (Number) Nodes ready.
- `total_nodes` (Number) Nodes expected.
- `updated_at` (String) Last change time, RFC 3339.

<a id="nestedatt--nodes"></a>
### Nested Schema for `nodes`

Required:

- `cloud` (String) Cloud the group runs in: `aws`, `gcp` or `azure`.
- `region` (String) Region the group runs in, for example `us-east-1`.
- `resources` (Attributes) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--nodes--resources))
- `tier` (String) Machine catalog name, for example `R20`. CPU and memory are derived from it; an unknown name is rejected. Changing it restarts the group's pods.

Optional:

- `count` (Number) Nodes in the group: one primary and `count - 1` replicas serving the read-only endpoint.

<a id="nestedatt--nodes--resources"></a>
### Nested Schema for `nodes.resources`

Read-Only:

- `cpu` (String) CPU request derived from `tier`.
- `memory` (String) Memory request derived from `tier`.



<a id="nestedatt--default_connections"></a>
### Nested Schema for `default_connections`

Optional:

- `admin` (Boolean) The admin user and its connection. Omitted, it is `true` on create and keeps its current value afterwards.
- `readonly` (Boolean) The read-only user and its connection. Omitted, it is `true` on create and keeps its current value afterwards.
- `readwrite` (Boolean) Not available: DocumentDB has no readwrite role; use readonly or admin.


<a id="nestedatt--storage"></a>
### Nested Schema for `storage`

Optional:

- `size` (String) Volume size, Kubernetes quantity, for example `20Gi`. It can only grow; a plan that shrinks it fails.


<a id="nestedblock--timeouts"></a>
### Nested Schema for `timeouts`

Optional:

- `create` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours).
- `delete` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours). Setting a timeout for a Delete operation is only applicable if changes are saved into state before the destroy operation occurs.
- `update` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours).


<a id="nestedatt--public_endpoints"></a>
### Nested Schema for `public_endpoints`

Read-Only:

- `host` (String)
- `port` (Number)
- `role` (String)

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
terraform import relay_documentdb_cluster.catalog <workspace_id>/<cluster_id>
```
